भ्रष्टाचारको मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ । सुनसरी र मोरङमा रहेको ‘रिजाल क्यानिङ एण्ड कम्पनी प्रा.ली.’ को नाममा रहेको सरकारी (हदबन्दी छुट पाएको) जग्गा सट्टापट्टा र बिक्री-वितरणमा व्यापक अनियमितता भएको भन्दै अख्तियारले ७३ करोड ४९ लाख ५६ हजार रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबीसहित आरोपपत्र दायर गरेको हो । यस प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री, मन्त्री, मुख्यसचिव, सचिवदेखि वडा सचिवसम्मका कर्मचारी र बिचौलियाहरूको मिलेमतोमा सरकारी जग्गा व्यक्तिको नाममा पुर्‍याएर बेचेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ । अख्तियारको अनुसन्धानले यो भ्रष्टाचार एउटा सुनियोजित र तहगत (तलदेखि माथिसम्मको) मिलेमतोमा भएको देखाएको छ । वि.सं. २०३२ सालमा तत्कालीन सरकारले रिजाल क्यानिङ एण्ड कम्पनी प्रा.ली.लाई फलफूल उद्योग सञ्चालन गर्ने सर्तमा ५९ बिघाभन्दा बढी जग्गा हदबन्दी छुट दिएर राख्न पाउने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर, कानुनअनुसार जुन सर्तमा जग्गा छुट दिइएको हो, त्यो सर्त पालना नभएमा (उद्योग नचलाएमा) उक्त जग्गा स्वतः नेपाल सरकारको नाममा जफत हुने व्यवस्था छ। रिजाल क्यानिङले सर्तअनुसार फलफूल उद्योग चलाएन । जग्गा बेवारिसे छाडियो । २०४८ सालमै सरकारले सर्त पालना नभएको भन्दै उक्त जग्गा जफत गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । मोरङको साबिक विराटनगर वडा नं. ३ (हाल महानगरपालिका) मा रहेको निकै महँगो जग्गा कम्पनीले निजी प्रयोगमा ल्याएको र बेवारिसे छाडेको भन्दै जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय मोरङ र भूमिसुधार कार्यालयले जग्गा जफत गर्ने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएका थिए । जग्गा जफत हुने निश्चित भएपछि कम्पनीका सञ्चालकहरूले कर्मचारीहरूसँग मिलेमतो सुरु गरे । विराटनगरको उक्त महँगो जग्गालाई ‘रूख र झाडी भएको, गाउँलेले फोहोर फाल्ने डम्पिङ साइट बनेको, लागूपदार्थ दुर्व्यसनीको अखडा बनेको’ भन्दै झुटो मुचुल्का र प्रतिवेदन तयार पारियो । कृषि र माटो परीक्षणका कर्मचारीलाई समेत मिलाएर उक्त जग्गा फलफूल खेतीका लागि अनुपयुक्त रहेको नक्कली सिफारिस बनाइयो । यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य विराटनगरको महँगो जग्गा बेच्ने र त्यसको सट्टामा अन्तै सस्तो जग्गा किनेर सरकारलाई देखाउने (सट्टापट्टा गर्ने) थियो । तलबाट मिलाइएको सेटिङ मन्त्रिपरिषद्‌सम्म पुग्यो । तत्कालीन मुख्यसचिव (माधव प्रसाद घिमिरे) र प्रधानमन्त्री माधव कुमार नेपालले उक्त जग्गा कानुनतः जफत हुनुपर्ने जान्दाजान्दै ‘सट्टापट्टा’ गर्न दिने प्रस्ताव मन्त्रिपरिषद्‌मा पेश गर्न लगाएको आरोपपत्रमा भनिएको छ । २०६६ मंसिरमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को सामाजिक समितिमा यो प्रस्ताव पुग्यो । उक्त समितिका संयोजक डा. मिनेन्द्र प्रसाद रिजाल थिए, जो कम्पनीका सञ्चालकहरूकै आफन्त पर्थे । स्वार्थको द्वन्द्व हुँदाहुँदै रिजालको समितिले सट्टापट्टा गर्न दिने निर्णय गर्‍यो र माधव नेपाल नेतृत्वको सरकारले त्यसलाई सदर गर्‍यो । मन्त्रिपरिषद्‌बाट अनुमति पाएपछि कम्पनीले मोरङको साबिक बनिगामा गाविसमा जम्मा १२ लाख ८५ हजार रुपैयाँमा खोला बगिरहेको, खाल्डो परेको सस्तो जग्गा किन्यो र त्यसलाई ‘सट्टापट्टा’ देखाएर विराटनगर महानगरपालिकाभित्रको बहुमूल्य जग्गा ८ करोड ३८ लाख ६२ हजार ५०० रुपैयाँमा बिक्री गर्‍यो । अख्तियारको मूल्याङ्कनअनुसार सरकारी सम्पत्ति हिनामिना हुँदा राज्यलाई कुल ७३ करोड ४९ लाख ५६ हजार रुपैयाँ घाटा लागेको छ । अख्तियारले यो प्रकरणमा संलग्न तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री माधव कुमार नेपाल र तत्कालीन मन्त्री डा. मिनेन्द्र प्रसाद रिजाललाई भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ अनुसार ७३ करोड ४९ लाख बिगो, त्यही बराबरको जरिवाना र कैद सजायको मागदाबी गरेको छ । यस प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन भूमिसुधार मन्त्री डम्बर श्रेष्ठ, मुख्यसचिव माधव प्रसाद घिमिरे लगायत केही सञ्चालक र कर्मचारीहरूको मृत्यु भइसकेकोले उनीहरूको हकमा सम्पत्ति जफतका लागि मात्र मुद्दा दायर गरिएको छ । रिजाल क्यानिङले षड्यन्त्रपूर्वक हात पारेर टुक्रा-टुक्रा पारी बेचेको उक्त विराटनगरको जग्गा हाल विभिन्न ६० भन्दा बढी व्यक्ति र संस्थाहरू (डेल्टा रियलटी, नेपाल स्वास्थ्य विकास तथा अनुसन्धान सहकारी संस्था लगायत) को नाममा छ । अख्तियारले ती सबै हालका जग्गाधनीहरूलाई पनि प्रतिवादी बनाउँदै उनीहरूको नाममा रहेको सरकारी जग्गा जफत गर्ने प्रयोजनका लागि मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ । Kathmandu. The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed a corruption case against 97 people, including former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, in a special court. The CIAA has filed a chargesheet claiming a loss of Rs 734.956 crore, alleging widespread irregularities in the exchange, sale and distribution of government land (exempt from restrictions) in the name of 'Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd.' in Sunsari and Morang. In this case, the Authority claims that government land was sold in the name of a private individual with the collusion of the then Prime Minister, ministers, Chief Secretary, employees ranging from secretaries to ward secretaries, and middlemen. The Authority's investigation has shown that this corruption was well-planned and involved collusion at various levels (from the bottom to the top). In 2032 BS, the then government had decided to allow Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd. to keep more than 59 bighas of land with a concession on the condition of operating a fruit industry. However, according to the law, if the condition on which the land concession was granted is not followed (if the industry is not operated), the land will automatically be confiscated in the name of the Government of Nepal. Rijal Canning did not operate the fruit industry as per the terms. The land was left unclaimed. In 2048 BS, the government decided to confiscate the land, saying that the terms were not met. The District Police Office, Morang and the Land Reforms Office had initiated the process of confiscating the very expensive land located in the former Biratnagar Ward No. 3 (currently the Metropolitan City) of Morang, alleging that the company had taken it for private use and left it unattended. After it was determined that the land would be confiscated, the company's directors began colluding with the employees. A false deed and report were prepared stating that the expensive land in Biratnagar was 'covered with trees and bushes, had become a dumping site for villagers to throw garbage, and had become a den for drug addicts.' A fake recommendation was made by the agriculture and soil testing staff that the land was unsuitable for fruit cultivation. The main objective was to sell the expensive land in Biratnagar and buy cheaper land elsewhere and show it to the government (sattapatta). The arrangement made from below reached the Council of Ministers. The charge sheet states that the then Chief Secretary (Madhav Prasad Ghimire) and Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal knowingly submitted a proposal to the Council of Ministers to allow the land to be 'satta-patta', knowing that it should be confiscated legally. The proposal reached the Social Committee of the Council of Ministers in November 2008. The coordinator of the committee was Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who was a relative of the company's directors. Despite the conflict of interest, Rijal's committee decided to allow the swap, and the Madhav Nepal-led government approved it. After receiving permission from the Council of Ministers, the company bought cheap land with a flowing river and a pothole in the former Banigama VDC of Morang for a total of Rs. 1.285 million and sold it as a 'satta patta' to valuable land within Biratnagar Metropolitan City for Rs. 83.862 million. According to the assessment of the Authority, the state has suffered a total loss of Rs. 734.956 million due to the misappropriation of government property. The CIAA has demanded Rs 734.9 million in damages, an equivalent fine and imprisonment for the then Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and the then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who were involved in this case, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059 BS. In this case, a case has been filed only for the confiscation of assets in their case, as some directors and employees, including the then Land Reforms Minister Dambar Shrestha, Chief Secretary Madhav Prasad Ghimire, have already died. The Biratnagar land, which was fraudulently acquired by Rijal Canning and sold in pieces, is currently in the names of more than 60 different individuals and organizations (including Delta Realty, Nepal Health Development and Research Cooperative Organization). The CIAA has filed a case against all of these current landowners as defendants for the purpose of confiscating the government land in their names.

The CIAA has filed a chargesheet claiming a loss of Rs 734.956 crore, alleging widespread irregularities in the exchange, sale and distribution of government land (exempt from restrictions) in the name of 'Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd.' in Sunsari and Morang. In this case, the Authority claims that government land was sold in the name of a private individual with the collusion of the then Prime Minister, ministers, Chief Secretary, employees ranging from secretaries to ward secretaries, and middlemen. The Authority's investigation has shown that this corruption was well-planned and involved collusion at various levels (from the bottom to the top). In 2032 BS, the then government had decided to allow Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd. to keep more than 59 bighas of land with a concession on the condition of operating a fruit industry. However, according to the law, if the condition on which the land concession was granted is not followed (if the industry is not operated), the land will automatically be confiscated in the name of the Government of Nepal. Rijal Canning did not operate the fruit industry as per the terms. The land was left unclaimed. In 2048 BS, the government decided to confiscate the land, saying that the terms were not met. The District Police Office, Morang and the Land Reforms Office had initiated the process of confiscating the very expensive land located in the former Biratnagar Ward No. 3 (currently the Metropolitan City) of Morang, alleging that the company had taken it for private use and left it unattended. After it was determined that the land would be confiscated, the company's directors began colluding with the employees. A false deed and report were prepared stating that the expensive land in Biratnagar was 'covered with trees and bushes, had become a dumping site for villagers to throw garbage, and had become a den for drug addicts.' A fake recommendation was made by the agriculture and soil testing staff that the land was unsuitable for fruit cultivation. The main objective was to sell the expensive land in Biratnagar and buy cheaper land elsewhere and show it to the government (sattapatta). The arrangement made from below reached the Council of Ministers. The charge sheet states that the then Chief Secretary (Madhav Prasad Ghimire) and Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal knowingly submitted a proposal to the Council of Ministers to allow the land to be 'satta-patta', knowing that it should be confiscated legally. The proposal reached the Social Committee of the Council of Ministers in November 2008. The coordinator of the committee was Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who was a relative of the company's directors. Despite the conflict of interest, Rijal's committee decided to allow the swap, and the Madhav Nepal-led government approved it. After receiving permission from the Council of Ministers, the company bought cheap land with a flowing river and a pothole in the former Banigama VDC of Morang for a total of Rs. 1.285 million and sold it as a 'satta patta' to valuable land within Biratnagar Metropolitan City for Rs. 83.862 million. The CIAA has demanded Rs 734.9 million in damages, an equivalent fine and imprisonment for the then Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and the then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who were involved in this case, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059 BS. In this case, a case has been filed only for the confiscation of assets in their case, as some directors and employees, including the then Land Reforms Minister Dambar Shrestha, Chief Secretary Madhav Prasad Ghimire, have already died. The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed a corruption case against 97 people, including former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, in a special court. The CIAA has filed a chargesheet claiming a loss of Rs 734.956 crore, alleging widespread irregularities in the exchange, sale and distribution of government land (exempt from restrictions) in the name of 'Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd.' in Sunsari and Morang. In this case, the Authority claims that government land was sold in the name of a private individual with the collusion of the then Prime Minister, ministers, Chief Secretary, employees ranging from secretaries to ward secretaries, and middlemen. The Authority's investigation has shown that this corruption was well-planned and involved collusion at various levels (from the bottom to the top). In 2032 BS, the then government had decided to allow Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd. to keep more than 59 bighas of land with a concession on the condition of operating a fruit industry. However, according to the law, if the condition on which the land concession was granted is not followed (if the industry is not operated), the land will automatically be confiscated in the name of the Government of Nepal. Rijal Canning did not operate the fruit industry as per the terms. The land was left unclaimed. In 2048 BS, the government decided to confiscate the land, saying that the terms were not met. The District Police Office, Morang and the Land Reforms Office had initiated the process of confiscating the very expensive land located in the former Biratnagar Ward No. 3 (currently the Metropolitan City) of Morang, alleging that the company had taken it for private use and left it unattended. After it was determined that the land would be confiscated, the company's directors began colluding with the employees. A false deed and report were prepared stating that the expensive land in Biratnagar was 'covered with trees and bushes, had become a dumping site for villagers to throw garbage, and had become a den for drug addicts.' A fake recommendation was made by the agriculture and soil testing staff that the land was unsuitable for fruit cultivation. The main objective was to sell the expensive land in Biratnagar and buy cheaper land elsewhere and show it to the government (sattapatta). The arrangement made from below reached the Council of Ministers. The charge sheet states that the then Chief Secretary (Madhav Prasad Ghimire) and Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal knowingly submitted a proposal to the Council of Ministers to allow the land to be 'satta-patta', knowing that it should be confiscated legally. The proposal reached the Social Committee of the Council of Ministers in November 2008. The coordinator of the committee was Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who was a relative of the company's directors. Despite the conflict of interest, Rijal's committee decided to allow the swap, and the Madhav Nepal-led government approved it. After receiving permission from the Council of Ministers, the company bought cheap land with a flowing river and a pothole in the former Banigama VDC of Morang for a total of Rs. 1.285 million and sold it as a 'satta patta' to valuable land within Biratnagar Metropolitan City for Rs. 83.862 million. According to the assessment of the Authority, the state has suffered a total loss of Rs. 734.956 million due to the misappropriation of government property. The CIAA has demanded Rs 734.9 million in damages, an equivalent fine and imprisonment for the then Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and the then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who were involved in this case, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059 BS. In this case, a case has been filed only for the confiscation of assets in their case, as some directors and employees, including the then Land Reforms Minister Dambar Shrestha, Chief Secretary Madhav Prasad Ghimire, have already died. The Biratnagar land, which was fraudulently acquired by Rijal Canning and sold in pieces, is currently in the names of more than 60 different individuals and organizations (including Delta Realty, Nepal Health Development and Research Cooperative Organization). The CIAA has filed a case against all of these current landowners as defendants for the purpose of confiscating the government land in their names.

The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed a corruption case against 97 people, including former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and then Minister Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, in a special court. The CIAA has filed a chargesheet claiming a loss of Rs 734.956 crore, alleging widespread irregularities in the exchange, sale and distribution of government land (exempt from restrictions) in the name of 'Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd.' in Sunsari and Morang. In this case, the Authority claims that government land was sold in the name of a private individual with the collusion of the then Prime Minister, ministers, Chief Secretary, employees ranging from secretaries to ward secretaries, and middlemen. The Authority's investigation has shown that this corruption was well-planned and involved collusion at various levels (from the bottom to the top). In 2032 BS, the then government had decided to allow Rijal Canning & Company Pvt. Ltd. to keep more than 59 bighas of land with a concession on the condition of operating a fruit industry. However, according to the law, if the condition on which the land concession was granted is not followed (if the industry is not operated), the land will automatically be confiscated in the name of the Government of Nepal. Rijal Canning did not operate the fruit industry as per the terms. The land was left unclaimed. In 2048 BS, the government decided to confiscate the land, saying that the terms were not met. The District Police Office, Morang and the Land Reforms Office had initiated the process of confiscating the very expensive land located in the former Biratnagar Ward No. 3 (currently the Metropolitan City) of Morang, alleging that the company had taken it for private use and left it unattended. After it was determined that the land would be confiscated, the company's directors began colluding with the employees. A false deed and report were prepared stating that the expensive land in Biratnagar was 'covered with trees and bushes, had become a dumping site for villagers to throw garbage, and had become a den for drug addicts.' मन्त्रिपरिषद्‌बाट अनुमति पाएपछि कम्पनीले मोरङको साबिक बनिगामा गाविसमा जम्मा १२ लाख ८५ हजार रुपैयाँमा खोला बगिरहेको, खाल्डो परेको सस्तो जग्गा किन्यो र त्यसलाई ‘सट्टापट्टा’ देखाएर विराटनगर महानगरपालिकाभित्रको बहुमूल्य जग्गा ८ करोड ३८ लाख ६२ हजार ५०० रुपैयाँमा बिक्री गर्‍यो । अख्तियारको मूल्याङ्कनअनुसार सरकारी सम्पत्ति हिनामिना हुँदा राज्यलाई कुल ७३ करोड ४९ लाख ५६ हजार रुपैयाँ घाटा लागेको छ ।

अख्तियारले यो प्रकरणमा संलग्न तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री माधव कुमार नेपाल र तत्कालीन मन्त्री डा. मिनेन्द्र प्रसाद रिजाललाई भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ अनुसार ७३ करोड ४९ लाख बिगो, त्यही बराबरको जरिवाना र कैद सजायको मागदाबी गरेको छ ।

यस प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन भूमिसुधार मन्त्री डम्बर श्रेष्ठ, मुख्यसचिव माधव प्रसाद घिमिरे लगायत केही सञ्चालक र कर्मचारीहरूको मृत्यु भइसकेकोले उनीहरूको हकमा सम्पत्ति जफतका लागि मात्र मुद्दा दायर गरिएको छ ।

रिजाल क्यानिङले षड्यन्त्रपूर्वक हात पारेर टुक्रा-टुक्रा पारी बेचेको उक्त विराटनगरको जग्गा हाल विभिन्न ६० भन्दा बढी व्यक्ति र संस्थाहरू (डेल्टा रियलटी, नेपाल स्वास्थ्य विकास तथा अनुसन्धान सहकारी संस्था लगायत) को नाममा छ । अख्तियारले ती सबै हालका जग्गाधनीहरूलाई पनि प्रतिवादी बनाउँदै उनीहरूको नाममा रहेको सरकारी जग्गा जफत गर्ने प्रयोजनका लागि मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ ।

A false deed and report were prepared stating that the expensive land in Biratnagar was 'covered with trees and bushes, had become a dumping site for villagers to throw garbage, and had become a den for drug addicts.' A fake recommendation was made by the agriculture and soil testing staff that the land was unsuitable for fruit cultivation. The main objective was to sell the expensive land in Biratnagar and buy cheaper land elsewhere and show it to the government (sattapatta). The arrangement made from below reached the Council of Ministers. The charge sheet states that the then Chief Secretary (Madhav Prasad Ghimire) and Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal knowingly submitted a proposal to the Council of Ministers to allow the land to be 'satta-patta', knowing that it should be confiscated legally. The proposal reached the Social Committee of the Council of Ministers in November 2008. The coordinator of the committee was Dr. Minendra Prasad Rijal, who was a relative of the company's directors. Despite the conflict of interest, Rijal's committee decided to allow the swap, and the Madhav Nepal-led government approved it. After receiving permission from the Council of Ministers, the company bought cheap land with a flowing river and a pothole in the former Banigama VDC of Morang for a total of Rs. 1.285 million and sold it as a 'satta patta' to valuable land within Biratnagar Metropolitan City for Rs. 83.862 million. According to the assessment of the Authority, the state has suffered a total loss of Rs. 734.956 million due to the misappropriation of government property. In this case, a case has been filed only for the confiscation of assets in their case, as some directors and employees, including the then Land Reforms Minister Dambar Shrestha, Chief Secretary Madhav Prasad Ghimire, have already died. The Biratnagar land, which was fraudulently acquired by Rijal Canning and sold in pieces, is currently in the names of more than 60 different individuals and organizations (including Delta Realty, Nepal Health Development and Research Cooperative Organization).
